title: Mitigate prorated session truncation causing lost customer credits across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Priya Kaur
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported net-negative or mysteriously low billed token usage following short-lived inference sessions that were terminated by autoscaler evictions, rate-limiter backpressure, or proxy reconnects. Root cause analysis shows the metering pipeline treats truncated sessions as full sessions but then applies a proration step that can drop the final partial-window contribution, effectively suppressing the last N-frames of tokens from the ledger. This impacts Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments because the same metering aggregator and proration logic runs in each mode.

Observed symptoms:
- Customers see lowered monthly usage compared to observed billing dashboards (delta ~0.5%–4% depending on workload).
- Discrepancies spike during high autoscale churn and bursty traffic (short-lived sessions, time < 60s).
- Backfill attempts double-count some sessions when correction jobs re-ingest truncated records.

Reproduction steps / how discovered:
1) Run a bursty test workload with short chats and aggressive client-side retries while forcing node preemption on Dedicated pools.
2) Observe token accounting emitted from serving runtime vs. aggregated ledger exports.
3) Compare final ledger after proration step and note that sessions ending mid-window often lose their trailing token bucket.

Why it matters: Lost credits affect customer trust and billing correctness. For some high-frequency customers this leads to escalations and manual refunds/backfills, increasing ops cost.

Scope: Hosted API + Redwood Dedicated + Private deployments (KMS rotation and on-prem edge route present same behavior).
acceptance_criteria: Metering pipeline must count tokens deterministically for sessions that end mid-window (no silent drop of trailing tokens)
Backfill job should idempotently apply corrections with no double-counts (reconciliation tests pass)
End-to-end e2e test across Hosted/Dedicated/Private showing <0.01% variance between runtime emitted tokens and final ledger for bursty short sessions
Alerting added for sudden rise in truncated-session-proration events and automated incident runbook created
implementation_notes: Adjust proration algorithm: move from 'discard trailing partial window when < X tokens' to 'proportional allocate fractional-window tokens to session ledger'
Introduce explicit session termination marker emitted by serving runtime on disconnect/eviction and surface it through proxy to metering-collector
Change aggregator to retain 'session-id + sequence-range' to prevent backfill double application; use monotonic session nonce to dedupe
Add a reconciliation worker that compares runtime token stream with ledger daily and emits a correction file for customers with >0.2% delta
Update private deployment docs with upgrade notes for metering microservice and migration plan for running one-time backfill job
risks_and_tradeoffs: Allocating fractional-window tokens increases per-customer invoice fidelity but slightly raises the complexity of aggregation math and test surface
Retaining session sequence ranges increases state held in aggregator; will add memory pressure for very high concurrency tenants — mitigated via TTL and sampling for low-volume customers
One-time backfill must be throttled for Dedicated clusters to avoid overload; will require an opt-in/off window for Private customers
timeline: Week 1: instrumentation + tests; Week 2: change proration logic + internal e2e; Week 3: deploy to canary Hosted and Dedicated; Week 4: run controlled backfills + broad rollout
